metadata.content: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Paris Fury retracts claim her husband has been diagnosed with schizophrenia | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Paris Fury retracts claim her husband has been diagnosed with schizophrenia Paris Fury says Tyson did not receive a diagnosis of schizophrenia; Netflix documentary has now been updated; The British Boxing Board of Control indicated it would look into comments about a schizophrenia diagnosis and could deny Fury a licence to face Anthony Joshua on December 11 Thursday 26 November 2026 23:20, UK Image: Tyson Fury has previously spoken about his struggles with mental health Paris Fury has retracted her claim that husband Tyson Fury was diagnosed with schizophrenia. A new Netflix documentary explores Tyson Fury's experiences of depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder, which became particularly acute after his unified heavyweight championship victory over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. Paris Fury made the comments about schizophrenia in an initial version of the documentary. Netflix said it has worked to "update" the footage in light of her clarification. She has now said: "I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson's condition and I used the word 'schizophrenic'. messages.text: Taylor and Lewis suffer five straight defeats on Modus Super Series return

metadata.summary: Phil 'The Power' Taylor and Adrian Lewis suffered five losses from five matches for England at Thursday's Modus Super Series International Pairs Tournament in Portsmouth.
metadata.content: Phil Taylor and Adrian Lewis suffer five straight defeats at Modus Super Series International Pairs | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Phil Taylor and Adrian Lewis suffer five straight defeats at Modus Super Series International Pairs Phil Taylor came out of retirement to partner Adrian Lewis for England at Thursday's Modus Super Series International Pairs Tournament in Portsmouth, but the duo endured a disappointing return, losing all five of their matches; Taylor retired from professional darts in 2018 Thursday 26 November 2026 19:03, UK Image: Phil Taylor (left) and Adrian Lewis suffered defeat in all five matches they played in Thursday's Modus Super Series International Pairs Tournament Phil 'The Power' Taylor and Adrian Lewis suffered five losses from five matches for England at Thursday's Modus Super Series International Pairs Tournament in Portsmouth. Taylor, now 66, retired from the competitive circuit in 2018, five years after claiming his 16th and final world title. However, the 16-time world champion returned to action to partner his long-time friend Lewis for the tournament. Their opening match on Thursday saw them face Scotland's John Henderson and Robert Thornton, with the England pair suffering a narrow 4-3 defeat. Things failed to improve in their second outing, as Taylor and Lewis were beaten 4-2 by Sweden's Andreas Harrysson and Anton Ostlund. metadata.content: Charles Leclerc denies presence of 'No 1 driver' clause in Ferrari contract as he and Lewis Hamilton hold 'good discussions' after collision | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Charles Leclerc denies presence of 'No 1 driver' clause in Ferrari contract as he and Lewis Hamilton hold 'good discussions' after collision Lewis Hamilton, meanwhile, confirms they remain "free to race" after talks following their collision in Las Vegas, for which Leclerc was punished by stewards; watch the Qatar GP on Sky Sports F1 this weekend, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday Thursday 26 November 2026 18:13, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Despite crashing with one another in Las Vegas, Lewis Hamilton says he's 'still free to race' against Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc Charles Leclerc has strongly denied suggestions he has a No 1 driver clause in his Ferrari contract. The Monegasque, who has been with the team since 2019 and signed an extended deal earlier this year, was speaking ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix as both he and Lewis Hamilton faced the media again four days on from their latest clash at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty by the stewards for causing a collision as he attempted to overtake Hamilton for sixth place in Las Vegas, with the incident also earning him severe criticism from Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur.
